company.name: Loopcart
company.description: Marketplace for refurbished phones, laptops and consoles, sold by vetted refurbishers with a one-year warranty.

title: Loopcart: more buyers than listings
brief: Loopcart's traffic is up after a TV mention, but conversion is flat: buyers search, do not find what they want and leave. Sellers complain that listing an item takes too long and that they never know when they will be paid. Plan a two-week sprint that turns the extra traffic into orders.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 20 tickets, 4 are traps and 1 critical problem is filed as minor. The best sprint delivers 652 points of value with 10 tickets, using 31 of 32 story points.
hidden.principle: Value per point, not value alone. A small sure win usually beats a large uncertain one.

stakeholders.name: Rafael
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Sofia
priorities: Keep the top sellers on the platform
Bring in large sellers this quarter
Never tell a seller 'we cannot do that'

stakeholders.name: Erik
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Tomás
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Amara
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

stakeholders.name: Marta
priorities: Disputes and payouts resolved on time

tickets.title: TLS certificate for the API expires in 9 days
tickets.description: Automatic renewal broke after the DNS move. When the certificate expires, every integration and the mobile clients stop connecting.

hidden.explanation: A total outage with a known date and a tiny fix. It is in the sprint before anything else is discussed.

tickets.title: Referral programme with rewards
tickets.description: Give users credit for every friend they bring. Referrals could double our signups.

hidden.explanation: It might work, but the claim has no baseline: nobody knows how many users refer today. A share link and a week of data would tell.

tickets.title: Badges and streaks for power users
tickets.description: Reward the most active users with badges, levels and streak counters. Engagement will go through the roof.

visible.impactHint: Engagement will go through the roof.

hidden.explanation: Decorates users who are already engaged. It does nothing for the ones who are leaving, which is where the metric problem is.

tickets.title: Saved searches with alerts
tickets.description: Buyers looking for something specific come back and repeat the same search. An alert would bring them back when it is listed.

hidden.explanation: A dependable retention feature for buyers with intent. Mid value, mid cost.

tickets.title: Cut deploy time from 50 minutes to 10
tickets.description: A deploy blocks the pipeline for almost an hour, so fixes are batched and hotfixes are slow.

visible.impactHint: The team deploys twice a week instead of daily.

hidden.explanation: Speeds up every release and every hotfix. Good value, but not a small job.

tickets.title: Remove the legacy v1 API code
tickets.description: No client has called v1 since March, but its code paths still have to be kept compiling and tested.

hidden.explanation: Tidy and safe to do, but nothing gets worse if it waits another sprint.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Search: typo tolerance and recent items
tickets.description: Search only matches exact words. One in five queries returns nothing, and most of those are misspellings of things that exist.

hidden.explanation: A real, measured friction for regular users. Solid mid-value work, though not cheap.

tickets.title: Weekly summary email
tickets.description: A short email every Monday with what happened in the account and one suggested action.

visible.impactHint: Our re-engagement emails get a 31% open rate.

hidden.explanation: A reasonable retention lever built on a channel that already works.

tickets.title: Special commission rules for Arbor & Finch
tickets.description: Arbor & Finch negotiated tiered commissions by category and month. Billing would need custom logic just for their account.

visible.impactHint: Already agreed verbally with Arbor & Finch.

hidden.explanation: A private deal hard-coded into billing. A credit note each month delivers the same discount with no code.

tickets.title: Stop the flood of payment-date emails to operations
tickets.description: The operations inbox gets dozens of emails a day from sellers asking when they will be paid. Sellers need a place to check their payout status themselves.

hidden.explanation: Same work as LOOP-377 ("Payout tracker for sellers"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Board dashboard with weekly KPIs
tickets.description: The CEO assembles the board numbers by hand from three tools every month. A dashboard would give them live.

hidden.explanation: Saves one person a couple of hours a month. Real but small, and no customer ever sees it.

tickets.title: Unsubscribe link shows a blank page in some email clients
tickets.description: A handful of recipients say the unsubscribe link does nothing in Outlook. They are still receiving our emails.

hidden.explanation: Ignoring unsubscribe requests breaks anti-spam law and gets sending domains blocklisted, which would also stop receipts and password resets.

tickets.title: Login loop on Safari since last Tuesday's release
tickets.description: Safari users are sent back to the login page after entering correct credentials. There is no workaround except switching browser.

hidden.explanation: A large group of users is locked out of the product by a regression. That is an incident, not a backlog item.

tickets.title: Filter search results by price, condition and delivery time
tickets.description: Buyers can only sort by date. They page through results looking for something in their budget, then leave.

visible.impactHint: 27% of searches end without a click.

hidden.explanation: Search is how buyers find anything. A quarter of searches lead nowhere, and the fix is well understood.

tickets.title: Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late
tickets.description: Reset emails sit in a low-priority queue behind marketing sends. Users request the email several times, then write to support or give up.

hidden.explanation: A cheap fix for one of the top support drivers. Users who cannot log in do not complain for long: they leave.

tickets.title: Favourites list
tickets.description: Buyers want to keep items they are considering. Today they leave tabs open or send links to themselves.

hidden.explanation: Expected by buyers and simple, though it does not change much on its own.

tickets.title: Bulk edit and bulk delete in list views
tickets.description: Power users clean up their data one row at a time. Some send support a spreadsheet and ask us to do it for them.

hidden.explanation: Saves real time for the heaviest users and removes a recurring support task.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Payout tracker for sellers
tickets.description: Sellers cannot see when their money will arrive, so they ask. The answer is always in the same internal table.

visible.impactHint: 'Where is my money?' is 22% of seller tickets.

hidden.explanation: Removes a fifth of seller tickets by showing data that already exists. High return for three points.

midSprintEvents.title: Samir is out for the rest of the sprint
midSprintEvents.description: Samir, one of the senior engineers, is on unexpected leave from today. Their work in progress has to be picked up by the rest of the team.

hidden.guidance: Capacity dropped, so scope has to drop with it. Cut the lowest-value work and protect the critical tickets. Asking the team to absorb the difference is how sprints fail quietly.
